item.title: Layback 0.6
item.description:
Layback 0.6

  • Runs on macOS 12 Monterey as well (0.5 needed macOS 13 and would not open there). The Audit window and the sidebar use what Monterey has; everything else is the same. On Monterey the Accessibility hint says System Preferences, as it is called there.
  • Live: a group left **unfolded** in the set is exported with each of its tracks as well, one file per track, named with the track at the end ("EMO - machael mix - MSTR v1 - VOX - Vocal.wav") and placed in the group's folder next to the group's own file. Fold the group and only the group is rendered, as before. The Groups picker shows "unfolded · + n" on such groups and the row says what it will render.
  • Live: selecting a track waits for Live's tick before checking, so a queue no longer trips on a selection that had not landed yet.

item.title: Layback 0.5
item.description:
Layback 0.5

  • Ableton Live, next to Pro Tools: Setup starts with a Platform step, and the rest of Layback follows the choice. A Live queue takes `.als` sets and renders each **group** of a set as its own file (Drums, Bass, Synths, Vocals…), named by your scheme with the group's suffix and put in the folder you give the group (Stems/Drums), then uploaded to Samply like any bounce. The set is never saved.
  • How it works: Live has no scripting for exporting, so Layback reads the set (tracks, groups, length) through the Layback link, a small remote script (AbletonOSC, bundled, installed from Setup into Live's Remote Scripts folder and chosen as a Control Surface), selects each group and works Live's own Export Audio/Video dialog for you through macOS Accessibility: opens it, checks its settings, presses Export, points the save panel at the right folder, types the name, presses Save, and waits for the render. Set the dialog once in Live (Rendered Track › Selected Tracks Only, your file type, bit depth and sample rate) and Layback uses it from then on; the log shows what the dialog was set to. The range is what the dialog proposes: the arrangement's time selection when there is one, else the whole set.
  • What it needs: Live 12 (its Export dialog and save panel are readable by Accessibility; verified on 12.4), the link enabled in Live's Settings › Link, Tempo & MIDI, and Layback allowed under System Settings › Privacy & Security › Accessibility. Live's window comes to the front while a group is exported. The Live link card in Setup and the inspector shows all three.
  • Groups list: the row names the group (or any track; `*` matches any text), its suffix and folder; once a set is read, tick its groups in the picker and a row per group is made. Add Common Groups offers Drums, Bass, Synths, Guitars, Vocals and FX as starting points.
  • `layback-cli live-probe` (what Live reports over the link), `live-export <group> <folder>` (one real export, to check the chain) and `live-demo` (the fake Live).
  • Not in this version: a range of Layback's own (the dialog's start and length follow Live's time selection, which the link cannot make), and Live's mix-down versions by muting (the Pro Tools way); Live users deliver groups.

item.title: Layback 0.4
item.description:
Layback 0.4

  • Stems: a version can record instead of bouncing. Give it Record tracks (the print tracks of your template, `SongTitle *`), and Layback arms them, records between the START and END markers in real time, and takes each track's file out of the session as its own stem, named by your scheme with the stem at the end: "Night Drive - machael mix - MSTR v1 - DRUMS". The fixed part of the pattern is dropped from the stem name, so no renaming in the Finder afterwards.
  • Stems that carried nothing are left out: Pro Tools' scripting link has no meters, so every recorded take is measured and a print track whose peak stays under -80 dBFS (Output › Stems) is not delivered; its take is deleted when the session closes unsaved. Nothing is armed afterwards, and the transport's record button goes back the way it was.
  • The track picker has a Record mode next to Mute and Solo (audio and instrument tracks only; an aux has no record button, so a stem printed through an aux needs an audio track fed from the same bus). The Audit window lists recorded stems with their level.
  • Stems need a range: with no START/END markers and no selection the stems version is reported as failed and the other versions go on.

item.title: Layback 0.3
item.description:
Layback 0.3

  • New name, same app. The layback is the last step before a mix goes out, which is where this app sits. The website is machael.studio/layback and updates come from machaelstudio/layback-releases.
  • A new icon: the queue on a dark purple glass tile, two sessions printed and the third playing.
  • Everything comes along on the first launch: the queue, the audit trail, the licence and the Samply connection (the BounceQueue folder in Application Support is renamed to Layback), and the profile and setup flag BounceQueue kept are read when Layback has none yet.
  • Keys: new keys start with LB-. A BQ- key issued before the rename keeps working as a Layback key; the portal lists it under Layback.
  • An installed BounceQueue 0.2 cannot update itself into Layback (the app's identity changed): download Layback once, drag it into Applications and delete the old app. Logs now go to ~/Library/Logs/Layback.
  • For scripts: the command-line tool is `layback-cli` and the hooks are `LAYBACK_*` (`LAYBACK_FAKE`, `LAYBACK_VIEW`, `LAYBACK_QUEUE`…).

item.title: BounceQueue 0.2
item.description:
BounceQueue 0.2

  • Your tag and mix label on every file: `{tag}` ("machael mix") and `{label}` ("MSTR v1") are set once in setup or the inspector, and each version has a short suffix (INST, ACA, TV) for `{suffix}`; the main mix has none. The standard scheme is now `{session} - {tag} - {label} - {suffix}`; existing queues keep their scheme until you pick "Use the standard scheme" in the tokens popover.
  • Audit window (toolbar clock, ⌥⌘A): a timeline of every bounce and upload with time, file, destination and duration, grouped by day, with filters, search, Finder and Samply links, CSV export and Clear History. Kept in `~/Library/Application Support/BounceQueue/audit.jsonl`.
  • Upload button in the toolbar next to Run Queue: a popover with the Samply uploads in progress (per-file progress), what finished and what failed.
  • Version rows can be edited by clicking straight into the name, suffix or track fields; the row the track picker follows is marked with a tint instead of list selection. Typing in them no longer stutters: the fields update the queue a moment after you stop typing.
  • The setup window stays away once finished or skipped, even after the app's identity changed (the flag is now kept in the queue file too).
  • Your account in the toolbar: click your name for the license, Settings (profile, this Mac's name, behaviour, Samply, updates), the Audit window and setup. Licensing works like PlugVault and Vessel, from the same Machael Studio portal: a 14-day trial, then a BQ- key with 3 seats; queues can still be set up without one, bouncing needs it.
  • In-app updates through Sparkle (weekly check, BounceQueue › Check for Updates…), and a release script that builds the disk image, signs and notarizes it, and publishes it with the appcast to machaelstudio/bouncequeue-releases.
  • Folder access prompts: the app's Info.plist was missing its closing tag, so macOS could not read the bundle identifier and had nothing to remember a folder grant against; it asked again at every access. Fixed, and `build.sh` now signs with your Apple Development certificate when one is available, so grants survive rebuilds and the keychain accepts the Samply token.
